questions.q: What does "subledger application" formally mean in Oracle Fusion?
options: Any custom report built in a subledger module
A module registered with Subledger Accounting, with its own event classes, event types, and sources
A synonym for the General Ledger
A spreadsheet used to manually track transactions
questions.explain: A subledger application is a formally registered module (like Payables or Fixed Assets) with its own SLA configuration of event classes, event types, and sources.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a source, in SLA terms?
options: The name of the Oracle Fusion data center
A specific piece of transaction data a rule can reference, such as the invoice amount or supplier name
The version number of the Fusion release
A user's login password
questions.explain: Sources are specific pieces of transaction data, like amount, supplier, or natural account, available for rules to reference.

questions.q: Why does a Fixed Assets depreciation event not offer a "Supplier Name" source, while a Payables invoice event does?
options: Because Fixed Assets is not a real subledger application
Because available sources are specific to the event class, and depreciation events have no supplier involved
Because supplier names are always hidden for security reasons
Because Oracle removed that feature in recent releases
questions.explain: Available sources depend entirely on the subledger application and event class; depreciation events offer sources relevant to assets, not suppliers.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what changes and what stays the same when a consultant moves from supporting Payables accounting to supporting Fixed Assets accounting?
options: Everything changes; nothing about SLA mechanics carries over between modules
Nothing changes at all; every module has identical sources and event classes
The rule-building mechanics stay the same across modules; what mainly changes is learning that module's specific sources and event classes
Fixed Assets does not use Subledger Accounting at all
questions.explain: Because every subledger application plugs into the same SLA engine with the same rule-building mechanics, the main new learning is each module's own sources and event classes.

questions.q: Which of the following modules were named in this lesson as registered subledger applications in Oracle Fusion?
options: Payables, Receivables, Fixed Assets, Cash Management, Cost Management, and Projects
Only Payables and Receivables; no other modules are SLA-enabled
Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Word
Only third-party, non-Oracle systems
questions.explain: The lesson lists Payables, Receivables, Fixed Assets, Cash Management, Cost Management, and Projects as examples of SLA-enabled subledger applications.
